points.title: 出生与早年
points.description: 1809年1月19日，爱伦·坡出生于波士顿，是演员夫妇大卫·坡和伊丽莎白·阿诺德的儿子。他的父母都是剧团演员，生活贫困。坡出生后不久，父亲离家出走，母亲在他两岁时因肺结核去世。坡成为孤儿后被约翰·爱伦夫妇收养，爱伦是富有的烟草商人。这段经历奠定了坡复杂的人生起点，也影响了他后来作品中常见的孤儿主题和死亡意象。
points.descriptionEn: Edgar Allan Poe was born on January 19, 1809, in Boston to actor parents David Poe Jr. and Elizabeth Arnold Poe. His parents were struggling actors, living in poverty. Shortly after Poe's birth, his father abandoned the family, and his mother died of tuberculosis when he was two years old. Poe became an orphan and was taken in by John Allan and his wife, who were wealthy tobacco merchants. This formative experience influenced his later works, which often feature orphaned characters and themes of death and loss.

points.title: 大学教育
points.description: 1826年，17岁的坡进入弗吉尼亚大学学习古典语言和文学。尽管学业优秀，但因养父约翰·爱伦拒绝提供足够的经济支持，坡不得不通过赌博筹集学费，最终欠下巨额债务。这段经历导致他与养父关系破裂，也使他对债务和经济困境产生了深刻的恐惧。大学期间，他开始创作诗歌，但作品尚未成熟。这段教育经历为他后来的文学创作奠定了基础，同时也埋下了他一生与经济困境斗争的种子。
points.descriptionEn: In 1826, at the age of 17, Poe entered the University of Virginia to study classical languages and literature. Despite his academic excellence, his foster father John Allan refused to provide sufficient financial support, forcing Poe to gamble to cover his expenses, which resulted in substantial debts. This experience led to a permanent rift with his foster father and instilled in Poe a deep fear of financial instability. During this time, he began writing poetry, though his works were not yet mature. This educational period laid the foundation for his later literary career while also sowing the seeds of his lifelong struggle with financial difficulties.

points.placeEn: United States Military Academy at West Point
points.title: 军旅生涯
points.description: 1830年，在养父再次拒绝资助后，坡加入了美国陆军，后进入西点军校学习。军校生活纪律严明，与坡自由不羁的性格形成鲜明对比。期间，他创作了《军中歌谣》等早期作品。1831年，他与养父关系彻底破裂，被西点军校开除。这段军旅经历培养了他的纪律性，也让他更加坚定了投身文学创作的决心。离开军校后，他搬到巴尔的摩与亲戚同住，开始了更加专注的文学创作生涯，发表了《厄舍府的倒塌》等早期重要作品。
points.descriptionEn: In 1830, after his foster father once again refused financial support, Poe joined the U.S. Army and later entered the United States Military Academy at West Point. The disciplined military life contrasted sharply with Poe's free-spirited nature. During this time, he wrote early works such as 'The Cadet's Song.' In 1831, his relationship with his foster father completely deteriorated, and he was dismissed from West Point. This military experience instilled discipline in him and strengthened his resolve to pursue a literary career. After leaving the academy, he moved to Baltimore to live with relatives and began a more focused literary career, publishing important early works like 'The Fall of the House of Usher.'

points.title: 编辑生涯开始
points.description: 1835年，坡开始在里士满的《南方文学信使》杂志担任编辑工作。这是他职业生涯的重要转折点，使他能够接触文学圈并发表自己的作品。在此期间，他与表妹弗吉尼亚·克莱姆结婚，当时她年仅13岁。作为编辑，坡不仅发表了自己的诗歌和小说，还撰写了大量文学评论，展现了他敏锐的批评眼光。他提出的'为艺术而艺术'理念对后来的唯美主义运动产生了深远影响。然而，由于他与雇主在饮酒问题上的冲突以及编辑理念的分歧，他最终于1839年离开《南方文学信使》。
points.descriptionEn: In 1835, Poe began working as an editor for the Southern Literary Messenger in Richmond, marking a significant turning point in his career. This position allowed him to access literary circles and publish his own works. During this time, he married his 13-year-old cousin Virginia Clemm. As an editor, Poe not only published his own poetry and fiction but also wrote numerous literary reviews, demonstrating his sharp critical eye. His concept of 'art for art's sake' profoundly influenced later aesthetic movements. However, due to conflicts with his employer over drinking issues and editorial differences, he eventually left the Southern Literary Messenger in 1839.

points.title: 创作高峰期
points.description: 1840年至1844年，坡在费城度过了他创作生涯中最富成果的时期。他担任多家杂志的编辑，同时创作了大量经典作品。1841年，他发表了《莫格街谋杀案》，开创了现代侦探小说的先河。1842年，他创作了《红死病的面具》，展现了其独特的哥特风格。1843年，他发表了《金甲虫》和《泄密的心》，进一步巩固了他在文学界的地位。这一时期，他发展了自己独特的文学理论，强调作品的统一效果和精心设计的结构。然而，尽管创作丰收，他的经济状况依然困难，妻子弗吉尼亚的健康状况也日益恶化，为他的生活蒙上了阴影。
points.descriptionEn: From 1840 to 1844, Poe spent his most productive creative period in Philadelphia. He worked as an editor for several magazines while producing numerous classic works. In 1841, he published 'The Murders in the Rue Morgue,' pioneering the modern detective story. In 1842, he wrote 'The Masque of the Red Death,' showcasing his distinctive Gothic style. In 1843, he published 'The Gold-Bug' and 'The Tell-Tale Heart,' further solidifying his position in literary circles. During this period, he developed his unique literary theories, emphasizing the 'unity of effect' and carefully crafted structures. Despite this creative bounty, his financial situation remained precarious, and his wife Virginia's health deteriorated, casting a shadow over his life.

points.title: 晚年与逝世
points.description: 1845年，坡搬到纽约，这是他人生最后的阶段。同年，他发表了《乌鸦》，这首诗使他一举成名，但也未能改善他的经济状况。1847年，妻子弗吉尼亚因肺结核去世，这对坡造成了沉重打击。晚年，他健康状况恶化，酗酒问题加剧。1849年10月3日，坡被发现昏迷在巴尔的摩街头，随后被送往医院，四天后去世，年仅40岁。他的死因至今成谜，可能是酒精中毒、脑瘤、心脏病或其他疾病。坡的早逝使他未能看到自己作品的广泛影响，但他的文学遗产却在后世不断被重新发现和评价，成为美国文学史上最具影响力的作家之一。
points.descriptionEn: In 1845, Poe moved to New York, marking the final stage of his life. That same year, he published 'The Raven,' which brought him sudden fame but failed to improve his financial situation. In 1847, his wife Virginia died of tuberculosis, a devastating blow to Poe. In his later years, his health deteriorated, and his drinking problem worsened. On October 3, 1849, Poe was found unconscious on the streets of Baltimore, taken to a hospital, and died four days later at the age of 40. The cause of his death remains mysterious, possibly alcohol poisoning, a brain tumor, heart disease, or another illness. Poe's early death prevented him from witnessing the widespread impact of his works, but his literary legacy has been continuously rediscovered and evaluated, making him one of the most influential figures in American literary history.

appraisal.zh: 爱伦·坡被尊为美国文学史上最具创新精神的作家之一，其哥特式恐怖小说与侦探小说开辟了新领域，对心理阴暗面的探索、独特的叙事与象征手法深刻影响了后世，"为艺术而艺术"的主张挑战了文学须承担道德教化的观念，为唯美主义铺路。也有研究者指出，他的情节往往简单、人物单薄，诗歌技巧精湛而内容阴郁，"统一效果"的理论有时牺牲了复杂性，作品缺乏社会关怀，未触及奴隶制、工业化等当代重大问题。学界多将他视为美国浪漫主义的代表与哥特美学、心理分析的先驱。
appraisal.en: Poe is revered as one of the most innovative figures in American letters, his Gothic horror and detective fiction opening new territory; his exploration of the darker psyche and his narrative and symbolic techniques deeply influenced later writers, and his 'art for art's sake' stance challenged the demand that literature serve moral instruction, paving the way for aestheticism. Researchers also note that his plots are often simple and his characters thin, that his technically masterful poetry dwells on the morbid, that his 'unity of effect' sometimes sacrificed complexity, and that his work lacks social engagement with slavery or industrialization. Scholarship generally treats him as a key figure in American Romanticism and a precursor of Gothic aesthetics and psychological analysis.

supporter.zh: 爱伦·坡被尊为美国文学史上最具创新精神的作家之一，他的哥特式恐怖小说和侦探小说开创了文学新领域。支持者认为坡的作品深刻探索了人类心理的黑暗面，其独特的叙事技巧和象征手法对后世文学产生了深远影响。他的'为艺术而艺术'理念挑战了当时文学必须具有道德教条的观念，为唯美主义运动铺平了道路。坡对诗歌形式的革新和对恐怖美学的探索，使他成为现代文学不可或缺的先驱。
supporter.en: Poe is revered as one of the most innovative figures in American literary history, whose Gothic horror and detective stories pioneered new literary territories. Supporters argue that his works profoundly explore the darker aspects of human psychology, with his unique narrative techniques and symbolism exerting profound influence on later literature. His concept of 'art for art's sake' challenged the prevailing notion that literature must serve moral didacticism, paving the way for the aesthetic movement. Poe's innovations in poetic form and exploration of the aesthetics of terror make him an indispensable precursor to modern literature.

critic.zh: 批评者指出爱伦·坡的作品存在诸多局限：他的小说情节往往过于简单，人物塑造单薄，缺乏深度；他的诗歌技巧虽然精湛但内容常显阴郁；他的个人生活充满争议，包括酗酒问题和与未成年表妹的婚姻。此外，坡的文学理论过于强调'统一效果'，有时牺牲了作品的复杂性和多样性。批评者认为，尽管坡对恐怖文学有开创性贡献，但他的作品缺乏社会关怀，未能触及当时美国社会面临的重大问题，如奴隶制和工业化等。
critic.en: Critics point out several limitations in Poe's work: his plots are often overly simplistic, his characterizations thin and lacking depth, and his poetry, while technically masterful, frequently dwells on morbid themes. His personal life was marked by controversy, including his drinking problem and marriage to his underage cousin. Additionally, Poe's literary theories emphasizing 'unity of effect' sometimes sacrificed complexity and diversity in his works. Critics argue that while Poe pioneered horror literature, his works lack social engagement and fail to address major contemporary American issues such as slavery and industrialization.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，爱伦·坡被定义为美国浪漫主义文学的代表人物，也是哥特式恐怖小说和侦探小说的奠基人。他的作品超越了时代限制，影响了从波德莱尔到爱因斯坦的众多文化人物。在流行文化中，坡的形象常与神秘、忧郁和天才联系在一起，成为哥特美学的象征。他的死亡之谜和传奇人生进一步强化了这种文化符号。现代学术界重新评价坡的作品，不仅关注其文学成就，也研究其作品中的心理分析元素，认为他是弗洛伊德精神分析理论的先驱之一。
objective.en: In academic and popular culture, Poe is defined as a key figure in American Romanticism and the founder of Gothic horror and detective fiction. His works have transcended time, influencing diverse cultural figures from Baudelaire to Einstein. In popular culture, Poe is often associated with mystery, melancholy, and genius, becoming a symbol of Gothic aesthetics. The mystery surrounding his death and legendary life have further reinforced this cultural icon. Modern scholarship has reevaluated Poe's work, not only for its literary achievements but also for its psychological elements, considering him a precursor to Freudian psychoanalysis.

self.zh: 我写诗不是为了钱，也不是为了名声，也不是为了任何人，而是因为我内心有一种无法抑制的冲动，一种神圣的狂热。
self.en: I wrote a poem not for the sake of money, nor for the sake of fame, nor for the sake of anybody, but because I had a divine impulse to write it.
